kept.excerpt: Spain defeated Portugal 1-0 in the round of 16, with Mikel Merino scoring a late winner assisted by Ferran Torres. Spain returned to the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time in 16 years and would next face the United States or Belgium.
kept.relevance: The primary resolution authority confirms that Spain remained in contention after its round-of-16 match on the cutoff date.

kept.excerpt: Spain defeated Portugal 0-1 at Dallas Stadium thanks to Merino's goal in the 91st minute. Following this victory, Spain would face the winner of USA–Belgium in the quarter-finals on Friday, July 10, at 9:00 pm CEST.
kept.relevance: This dated official club report identifies Spain's next elimination hurdle and the scheduled date of that match.

kept.excerpt: Luis de la Fuente said Nico Williams had completed training with the group but was returning from an injury and a short period of inactivity. Whether Williams received minutes against Portugal would depend on the development of the match.
kept.relevance: The national federation's dated briefing provides direct evidence of an important attacking player's fitness limitations immediately before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Spain beat Austria 3-0 through two goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and one from Pedro Porro. It was Spain's first World Cup knockout victory since its title-winning run in 2010. Unai Simon's clean sheet was his fifth successive World Cup shutout, including the 2022 match against Morocco, and extended his run without conceding to 519 minutes.
kept.relevance: The official report documents Spain's attacking performance and defensive strength entering the later knockout rounds.

kept.excerpt: Spain sealed first place in Group H and eliminated Uruguay with a 1-0 victory. Alex Baena scored Spain's goal, and Uruguay's Agustin Canobbio received a stoppage-time red card for a challenge on Pau Cubarsi.
kept.relevance: The report establishes Spain's successful group-stage progression and provides evidence of its performance against Uruguay.

kept.excerpt: Cape Verde held Spain to a 0-0 draw on its World Cup debut. Lamine Yamal came off the bench in the second half, while Ferran Torres hit the crossbar before halftime. Spain entered the tournament after winning Euro 2024 but had failed to advance beyond the round of 16 in each of the previous three World Cups.
kept.relevance: Spain's opening match supplies counterevidence about finishing against a compact defence, alongside its recent European title and World Cup history.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-06, inclusive of articles dated that day; no narrower intraday cutoff was specified. Publication dates were verified from explicit dates in web-search results and indexed article text, rather than inferred from match dates alone. Spanish excerpts are translated factual summaries. web_fetch failed because of provider configuration; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback was rate-limited and returned no article bodies, so verification relies on indexed source text. Later-dated reporting, rolling pages containing subsequent developments, sources with unknown publication dates, and betting or prediction-market pages were excluded. No post-cutoff developments or tournament outcome are included.
